premises.text: The endpoint under investigation is process_file at /process/file in this Open WebUI revision.
The supplied input includes file_id and destination collection_name.
The caller may own the supplied file or the file may belong to another user.
Caller ownership of the destination collection is unspecified.

questions.request: Investigate process_file at /process/file in this Open WebUI revision. Trace the caller, the supplied file_id, and the destination collection_name through authorization and the eventual processing or vector write. Explain whether the object authorized for input and the object affected by output are the same, and what happens for a caller-owned file versus another user's file. Do not assume the caller owns the destination collection. Give visible conditions and specific remaining limits.

result.scope: open-webui/open-webui@841c9045d789005145274955e7ef60b1b11a9be9; allowed source scope backend/open_webui; traced retrieval router process_file and its visible save_docs_to_vector_db path, not all repository callers or deployment configuration

behavior.explanation: The endpoint is mounted under the retrieval router, whose visible prefix is /api/v1/retrieval, so the route is /api/v1/retrieval/process/file. It requires the verified-user dependency, then authorizes input-file lookup differently by role: admins use the unrestricted file-id lookup, while non-admins use file-id plus user-id. A found file is processed and its content/status/hash/collection metadata are updated; when embedding/retrieval is enabled, vector data is written to the supplied collection_name when one is supplied, without a visible destination-collection access check in this endpoint. Thus input-file authorization and destination-collection authorization are separate, and the visible code does not establish that they are the same object or that the caller owns the destination.

branches.condition: Non-admin caller owns file_id; form_data.collection_name is non-null; embedding/retrieval is enabled; processing and vector operations succeed.
branches.explanation: The non-admin lookup binds file_id to user.id. The explicit collection_name is retained and passed to save_docs_to_vector_db; add is set true, so an existing destination collection is eligible for insertion. The helper performs a hash-duplicate check and then inserts items into exactly that collection. No call to _validate_collection_access is visible in process_file, so caller ownership or write access to that destination is not established by this path.

branches.condition: Non-admin caller owns file_id; collection_name is omitted; embedding/retrieval is enabled; processing and vector operations succeed.
branches.explanation: The destination defaults to file-{file.id}. It is still passed to the vector-save helper, but add is false. If that collection already exists, the helper returns true without inserting; otherwise it generates embeddings and inserts the processed items into file-{file.id}. The default name is derived from the authorized input file, but this is an implementation naming relationship, not a visible collection ownership check.

branches.condition: Non-admin caller supplies a file_id belonging to another user, or otherwise not returned by the user-scoped lookup.
branches.explanation: The endpoint calls get_file_by_id_and_user_id(form_data.file_id, user.id), so another user's file is not selected. The visible else branch raises HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND when no file is found. Processing, file updates, and vector writes are therefore not reached through this endpoint for that branch.

branches.condition: Caller has role admin and supplies an existing other-user file_id.
branches.explanation: Admins use get_file_by_id(form_data.file_id), without the user-id restriction shown for non-admins, so an existing other-user file can enter the processing flow. The generated document metadata retains the file's file.id and file.user_id, while the destination remains the caller-supplied collection_name or the file-derived default. Destination collection ownership is still not checked in the visible process_file path.

branches.condition: A file is found and BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled.
branches.explanation: The endpoint updates the file content, marks the file completed, stores its hash, and returns collection_name as None before calling the vector-save helper. No vector write occurs in this branch, regardless of the supplied collection_name.

branches.condition: A found file reaches processing but loading, embedding, duplicate detection, or vector insertion fails.
branches.explanation: The helper can reject duplicate content when an existing hash is associated with a different file_id, and vector insertion targets the selected collection. The endpoint's outer error path marks the file failed, clears its hash, and returns a 400 (with a special Pandoc message), but the source does not show rollback of any external vector-side effects that may already have occurred.

result.scope: open-webui/open-webui@841c9045d789005145274955e7ef60b1b11a9be9; allowed source scope backend/open_webui; traced the registered retrieval route, process_file body, file lookup methods as used there, and the visible save_docs_to_vector_db effect path; this is not an all-repository or deployment-runtime review

behavior.explanation: The handler is registered as POST /process/file on the retrieval router, mounted at /api/v1/retrieval, and requires get_verified_user. It authorizes/selects the input file by supplied file_id: admins use an unrestricted ID lookup, while non-admins use file_id plus the verified caller's user.id. Once a file is selected, the handler may update that file's stored content, status, hash, and collection metadata. With retrieval enabled, it separately targets either the caller-supplied collection_name or the default file-{file.id}; the visible process_file path does not call the available collection-access validator before querying or writing that collection. Therefore the authorized input object is the file record, while the output object is a vector collection (and, in one content-update branch, an additional default collection is deleted). They are not the same authorization object. A non-admin's other-user file is short-circuited as not found, but a caller-owned file can be processed into an explicitly named destination whose ownership/write authorization is not established by this path; admins can process another user's existing file under the same destination behavior.

branches.condition: The caller is non-admin, file_id belongs to that caller, collection_name is supplied, embedding/retrieval is enabled, and processing succeeds.
branches.explanation: The user-scoped lookup binds the input file to user.id. The supplied collection_name is retained and passed unchanged to save_docs_to_vector_db with add=True. The helper queries that collection for the content hash and, unless duplicate-content logic rejects it, inserts generated vector items into that exact collection. If the collection already exists, add=True permits insertion. No _validate_collection_access call is visible on this route, so ownership of or write access to the destination is not established here.

branches.condition: The caller is non-admin, file_id belongs to that caller, collection_name is omitted, embedding/retrieval is enabled, and processing succeeds.
branches.explanation: The destination is derived as file-{file.id} and passed to the vector helper with add=False. If that collection already exists, the helper returns success without inserting because overwrite and add are both false; otherwise it embeds and inserts into file-{file.id}. The naming ties the destination to the authorized file identifier, but the visible code still performs no collection-ownership/write-access check.

branches.condition: A non-admin supplies a file_id owned by another user, or any ID not returned by the file_id-and-user_id lookup.
branches.explanation: The handler uses get_file_by_id_and_user_id(form_data.file_id, user.id). If it returns no file, the handler raises HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND, so content processing, file mutation, destination queries, and vector writes are not reached through this route.

branches.condition: The verified caller's role is admin and file_id identifies an existing file owned by another user.
branches.explanation: The admin branch uses get_file_by_id without binding the lookup to the caller's user.id, so the other user's file can enter processing. Generated metadata records the selected file's own user_id as created_by and its ID as file_id. The vector destination is still the supplied collection_name or file-{file.id}, with no visible destination-access validation in process_file.

branches.condition: A selectable file is found and form_data.content is truthy, whether or not an explicit collection_name is supplied.
branches.explanation: Before preparing the replacement content, the handler attempts to delete the default collection file-{file.id}; exceptions from that deletion are swallowed. If an explicit collection_name was also supplied and retrieval is enabled, the later save targets that supplied destination. Thus this branch can affect two different collection identities: deletion of file-{file.id} and insertion into the supplied collection_name.

branches.condition: A selectable file is found and BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled.
branches.explanation: The handler updates the selected file's content, status, and hash, then returns collection_name=None before save_docs_to_vector_db. No eventual vector insertion occurs in this branch, although the earlier content-supplied branch may already have attempted deletion of file-{file.id}.

branches.condition: An explicit destination collection already exists and the file reaches vector saving.
branches.explanation: Because process_file sets add=True whenever form_data.collection_name is supplied, the helper does not take its existing-collection early return and proceeds toward insertion. Before insertion, a same-hash record tied to a different file_id causes DUPLICATE_CONTENT; the same file_id is treated as re-add/reindex. These checks concern content/file identity, not caller authorization to the collection.

branches.condition: A selected file encounters a loader, empty-content, embedding, duplicate-content, or vector-operation exception.
branches.explanation: The outer error path marks the selected file failed, clears its hash, and raises HTTP 400 (with a special Pandoc-not-installed response). The visible code does not show compensating rollback for external vector effects that may have occurred before a later failure.
